authors: van der Leij, Broens, Hesselink, Schuurman, Vernooij, Egberink

mcqs.q: What SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence was found among the sampled Dutch shelter cats?
mcqs.e: Only 2 of 240 cats (0.8%) had confirmed neutralizing antibodies.

mcqs.q: On PCR testing, the two seropositive cats were:
mcqs.e: Both seropositive cats tested PCR negative, indicating no active shedding.

mcqs.q: The study concluded that shelter cats are:
o: unlikely to be a reservoir or significant public health risk
mcqs.e: Low seroprevalence and negative PCR support that shelter cats are an improbable reservoir.

mcqs.q: How did most clients rate their community veterinary program experience?
mcqs.e: The majority reported positive experiences with both services and communication.

mcqs.q: Which elements did the study emphasize as needed for successful community-based programs?
mcqs.e: Effective communication, empathy, and cultural competence were highlighted as key.

mcqs.q: The authors concluded low-cost/free community vet programs can:
o: open the door to future positive veterinary experiences for disadvantaged owners
mcqs.e: Such programs help disadvantaged owners access and value veterinary care going forward.

mcqs.q: Of cats assessed at least twice, what proportion showed deterioration in at least one health indicator?
mcqs.e: Deterioration in ≥1 indicator was recorded in 52 of 125 cats (41.6%).

mcqs.q: Length of stay (LOS) significantly predicted scores for which indicators?
o: abnormal posture/lameness and the upper respiratory index
mcqs.e: LOS predicted posture/lameness scores and a composite URI index.

mcqs.q: Cat age predicted scores for which indicators?
mcqs.e: Age predicted coat and body condition scores.

mcqs.q: What proportion of relinquishment requests resulted in acceptance of free behaviour advice?
mcqs.e: Advice was accepted in 24.4% of requests.

mcqs.q: Advice was most likely to be accepted for which problem type?
o: aggression between dogs in the home
mcqs.e: Odds of acceptance were ~5.8x higher for general management vs in-home dog aggression.

mcqs.q: The study concluded that behaviour advice at relinquishment:
o: could reduce relinquishment but its impact may be limited, so complementary solutions are also needed
mcqs.e: Owners accept advice, but limited uptake means proactive solutions are also required.

mcqs.q: Which enrichment was associated with body positions indicating lower stress during kennel cleaning?
mcqs.e: Calming enrichment lowered stress, with calming lavender scent most beneficial.

mcqs.q: Which item produced the greatest reduction in vocalization?
mcqs.e: The arousing ball showed the greatest vocalization reduction.

mcqs.q: A key conclusion regarding enrichment type was that:
o: enrichment other than food may be more effective for certain undesirable behaviours
mcqs.e: Non-food enrichment was more effective for some unwanted behaviours.

mcqs.q: A central management challenge for IOSD in shelters is that:
o: treatments effective in privately owned cats may be impractical or ineffective in shelters
mcqs.e: Owned/experimental-animal protocols often do not translate to the shelter setting.

mcqs.q: What does the review highlight about feline herpesvirus therapeutics?
o: discrepancies exist between experimental laboratory studies and clinical trials
lab and clinical results agree perfectly
mcqs.e: The review stresses divergence between lab-based studies and clinical trials for FHV.

mcqs.q: The review concluded that:
o: further high-quality clinical trials are needed to define optimal protocols
mcqs.e: Optimal preventive and therapeutic protocols still require high-quality trials.

authors: Stubing, Suchodolski, Reisinger, Werner, Hartmann, Unterer, Busch

mcqs.q: Comparing metronidazole vs a synbiotic for canine acute diarrhea, the clinical course (CADS index) showed:
mcqs.e: No significant clinical difference was seen (except CADS on a single day).

mcqs.q: Metronidazole's effect on the intestinal microbiome was to:
o: negatively impact it (lower C. hiranonis, higher E. coli)
mcqs.e: Metronidazole raised E. coli and lowered C. hiranonis versus the synbiotic.

mcqs.q: The authors concluded that:
o: metronidazole is the preferred first-line treatment
antibiotics are always indicated for acute diarrhea
synbiotics might be preferred over metronidazole for dogs with acute diarrhea
C. perfringens drives all acute diarrhea
mcqs.e: Because metronidazole harms the microbiome without clinical benefit, synbiotics may be preferred.

mcqs.q: Housing issues represented approximately what share of overall shelter intakes?
mcqs.e: Housing-related issues accounted for 14% (n=28,424) of intakes.

mcqs.q: Which animals were at greatest risk of euthanasia or shelter death?
o: pit bull-type dogs and animals relinquished by unhoused owners
mcqs.e: Pit bull-type dogs and animals from unhoused owners had elevated death risk.

mcqs.q: Over the 2019–2023 period, which longitudinal trend was observed?
o: intakes due to loss of home decreased
cat intakes decreased while dog intakes rose
intakes due to loss of home increased while pet-restriction and landlord intakes decreased
mcqs.e: Home-loss intakes rose; pet-restriction/landlord intakes (and pit bull share) fell.

mcqs.q: What was the most common intake source for rabbits at the BC SPCA?
o: owner surrender, mostly for human-related reasons
mcqs.e: Owner surrender (40.2%) led, with 96.9% surrendered for human-related reasons.

mcqs.q: What was the median length of stay for shelter rabbits?
mcqs.e: Median LOS was 29 days, underscoring a need to shorten time to adoption.

mcqs.q: What was the adoption outcome for these rabbits?
mcqs.e: 80.3% of rabbits were subsequently adopted.

authors: Campbell, Arnott, Graham, Niel, Ward, Ma

mcqs.q: Which foster-housing arrangement was associated with positive kitten behaviour?
o: isolated quiet rooms with no human contact
social areas of the house with less noise/activity and some time alone
mcqs.e: Social-area housing with lower noise plus some alone time predicted positive behaviour.

mcqs.q: For bottle-fed kittens, singletons, and queen-absent kittens, fear/anxiety responses were:
o: absent when the queen was present
mcqs.e: No difference in fear/anxiety was found for these groups.

mcqs.q: Ringworm treatment was associated with:
mcqs.e: Ringworm treatment correlated with more fearful kitten behaviour.

mcqs.q: Compared with short-term dogs, long-term shelter dogs were significantly more often:
o: a 'dangerous breed', male, and older at admission
mcqs.e: LT dogs were more often dangerous-breed, male, and older when admitted.

mcqs.q: How were long-term dogs rated on behaviour/personality?
o: higher aggression and high arousal with lower amicability
mcqs.e: LT dogs scored higher on aggression and arousal and lower on amicability.

mcqs.q: The formal welfare assessment protocol revealed that:
o: LT dogs scored markedly worse on welfare
LT dogs scored better on welfare
there was no welfare difference between LT and ST dogs
mcqs.e: Despite behavioural differences, welfare assessment showed no group difference.

mcqs.q: What happened to the dogs' baseline cortisol over the animal-assisted intervention (AAI) program?
o: it significantly decreased by program end
mcqs.e: Baseline cortisol significantly decreased by the end of the AAI program.

mcqs.q: What effect did transportation have on the dogs' cortisol?
mcqs.e: Transportation significantly raised cortisol, flagged as a critical phase.

mcqs.q: The authors concluded that AAI activities:
o: may improve the welfare of kenneled shelter dogs
should be avoided for shelter dogs
mcqs.e: Reduced baseline cortisol suggests AAI can improve kenneled dogs' welfare.
